introduction: DC TANF provides cash and supportive services for eligible families. DHS reviews family circumstances and financial eligibility.
description: DC TANF provides cash and supportive services for eligible families. DHS reviews family circumstances and financial eligibility.

sections.who: Applicants must meet District residency and qualifying family or pregnancy rules, with income and resource screening. Orientation, assessment and an Individual Responsibility Plan are part of the program.
sections.get: Support can include cash, employment and education coaching, child care and other family services. Exemptions from participation depend on circumstances.
sections.docs:
• Household, child or pregnancy information.
  • Income and resource records.
  • Evidence relevant to work barriers, disability or requested exemptions.
sections.apply:
1. Submit the application

    Use District Direct or the methods on DHS Public Benefits.

  2. Complete assessment

    Respond to evidence requests and attend Office of Work Opportunity orientation and assessment as directed.

  3. Develop the responsibility plan

    Discuss goals, supportive services and any exemption with the case worker.
sections.after: Keep appointments and notices. Announced TANF stabilization changes begin October 1, 2027, not October 2026; review preparation instructions if affected.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using DC TANF eligibility and current notices; DHS application and recertification. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Is TANF only a cash benefit?
No. DHS lists employment, education, child care and other supports.
Some circumstances qualify; discuss them with the case worker.
When do the announced changes begin?
Can a TANF-only renewal always be done online?
The current Public Benefits page says TANF-only recertification cannot be completed online; check instructions.
